'''Vahagn''' "'''Vahe'''" '''Gurzadyan''' ({{langx|hy|Վահագն Գուրզադյան}}; born 21 November 1955) is an Armenian [[mathematical physicist]] and a professor and head of Cosmology Center at [[Yerevan Physics Institute]], Yerevan<!-- DO NOT LINK, see [[MOS:GEOLINK]] for further guidance -->, Armenia<!-- DO NOT LINK, see [[MOS:GEOLINK]] for further guidance -->, best known for co-writing "[[Concentric circles]] in [[WMAP]] data may provide evidence of violent pre-Big-Bang activity"<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | last2 = Penrose | first2 = R. | year = 2013 | title = On CCC-predicted concentric low-variance circles in the CMB sky| journal = Eur. Phys. J. Plus| volume = 128 | issue = 2| page = 22 | doi=10.1140/epjp/i2013-13022-4| arxiv = 1302.5162| bibcode = 2013EPJP..128...22G| s2cid = 55249027 }}</ref>
paper with his colleague, [[Roger Penrose]], and collaborating on Roger Penrose's recent book ''[[Cycles of Time (book)|Cycles of Time]]''.

Gurzadyan was born in [[Yerevan]], [[Armenian SSR]]. He graduated from [[Yerevan State University]] (1977), was a postgraduate student in the theoretical physics department of the [[Lebedev Physics Institute]] at Moscow (1977–1980; 1980 PhD.), DSci in theoretical and mathematical physics (1988).

In 1989 he lectured on dynamical systems in four universities in Japan (Tokyo, Kyoto, Hiroshima, Fukui), and subsequently held visiting positions at the University of Sussex (1996–1997) and, since 2001, at [[Sapienza University of Rome]]. His father [[Grigor Gurzadyan]], an Armenian [[astronomer]], pioneered space-based astronomy using satellites. His grandfather [[Ashkharbek Kalantar]] was an archaeologist and historian, Fellow of the [[Russian Imperial Archaeological Society]], and the keeper of the [[Asiatic Museum]] in [[Saint Petersburg|St. Petersburg]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ysu.am/gender/en/The-bust-of-Ashkharbek-Kalantar-was-placed-at-YSU|title = The Bust of Ashkharhbek Kalantar Was Placed at Ysu}}</ref>

== Main research ==
The main topics of his research are chaos in non-linear systems, [[accretion (astronomy)|accretion]] onto massive [[black hole]]s, stellar dynamics, and observational cosmology.

Gurzadyan has papers predicting elliptical [[accretion disk]]s formed in galactic nuclei at tidal disruption of stars near massive black holes;<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | last2 = Ozernoy | first2 = L.M. | year = 1979 | title = Accretion on massive black holes in galactic nuclei | journal = Nature | volume = 280 | issue = 5719| pages = 214–215 | doi=10.1038/280214a0| bibcode = 1979Natur.280..214G | s2cid = 4306883 }}</ref> the tidal mechanism currently is associated to the flares observed in AGN.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Komossa | first1 = S. | year = 2015 | title = Tidal disruption of stars by supermassive black holes: Status of observations| journal = J. High Energy Astrophys. | volume = 7 | pages = 148–157 | doi= 10.1016/j.jheap.2015.04.006 | arxiv = 1505.01093| bibcode = 2015JHEAp...7..148K| s2cid = 119152755 }}</ref>

He has shown (with Savvidy; [[Gurzadyan–Savvidy relaxation]]) the exponential instability (chaos) in spherical stellar systems and has derived the collective relaxation time.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | last2 = Savvidy | first2 = G.K. | year = 1986 | title = Collective relaxation of stellar systems | journal = Astron. Astrophys. | volume = 160 | page = 203 | bibcode = 1986A&A...160..203G }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | last2 = Kocharyan | first2 = A.A. | year = 2009 | title = Collective relaxation of stellar systems revisited | journal = Astron. Astrophys. | volume = 505 | issue = 2| pages = 625–627 | doi=10.1051/0004-6361/200912218 | bibcode=2009A&A...505..625G| arxiv = 0905.0517 | s2cid = 8011915 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Vesperini | first1 = E | year = 1992 | title = Possible observational indication for Gurzadyan–Savvidy relaxation for globular clusters | journal = Astron. Astrophys. | volume = 266 | issue = 1| page = 215 | bibcode = 1992A&A...266..215V }}</ref> He has formulated a list of 10 key problems in stellar dynamics<ref>{{Cite book |arxiv=1407.0398 |last1=Gurzadyan|first1=V. G |chapter=10 key problems in stellar dynamics: In retrospect|title=Ergodic Concepts in Stellar Dynamics |editor1=V.G. Gurzadyan |editor2=D. Pfenniger |series=Lecture Notes in Physics |publisher=Springer |year=1994|volume=430|pages=281–291|bibcode=2014arXiv1407.0398G}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Eingorn | first1 = M. | year = 2014 | title = Gurzadyan's Problem 5 and improvement of softenings for cosmological simulations using the PP method | journal = Adv. High Energy Phys. | volume = 2014 | pages = 1–4 |arxiv=1409.0220 | doi=10.1155/2014/903642| bibcode = 2014arXiv1409.0220E | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | last2 = Harutyunyan | first2 = V.V. |last3 =Kocharyan | first3 = A.A. | year = 2015 | title = A principal possibility for computer investigation of evolution of dynamical systems with independent on time accuracy | journal = European Physical Journal C | volume = 75 | issue = 6| page = 252 | doi=10.1140/epjc/s10052-015-3479-5 | doi-access=free| arxiv = 1505.06741 | bibcode = 2015EPJC...75..252G | s2cid = 53581660 }}</ref> He has proved a theorem ([[Gurzadyan theorem]]) on the most general functional form for the force satisfying the condition of identity of the gravity of the sphere and of a point mass located in the sphere's center.<ref name=Gurzadyan>{{cite journal | last=Gurzadyan |first=Vahe |author-link=vahe Gurzadyan|title=The cosmological constant in McCrea-Milne cosmological scheme|journal=The Observatory|date= 1985|volume=105|pages=42–43|bibcode=1985Obs...105...42G}} http://adsabs.harvard.edu/full/1985Obs...105...42G</ref>

Cosmic microwave background indications for cosmic voids were obtained by Gurzadyan et al., including on the void nature of the [[CMB cold spot|Cold Spot]],<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | last2 = Kocharyan | first2 = A.A. | year = 2009 | title =  Porosity Criterion for Hyperbolic Voids and CMB | journal = Astron. Astrophys. | volume = 493 | issue = 3| pages = L61–63 | doi=10.1051/0004-6361:200811317 | bibcode=2009A&A...493L..61G| arxiv = 0807.1239 | s2cid = 55162500 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | year = 2014 | title =  To the center of cold spot with Planck | journal = Astron. Astrophys. | volume = 566 | pages = A135 | doi=10.1051/0004-6361/201423565 |display-authors=etal | bibcode=2014A&A...566A.135G| arxiv =1404.6347 | s2cid = 118519828 }}</ref> confirmed by independent galaxy survey,<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Szapudi | first1 = I. | year = 2015 | title =  Detection of a supervoid aligned with the cold spot of the cosmic microwave background | journal = Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society | volume = 450  | issue = 1 | pages = 288–294 | doi=10.1093/mnras/stv488 | doi-access = free |display-authors=etal| arxiv =1405.1566| bibcode =2015MNRAS.450..288S}}</ref> as of possibly the largest known structure in the Universe.

Gurzadyan has suggested and initiated the use of Compton Edge method for high accuracy testing of the light speed isotropy and the [[Lorentz invariance]] at GRAAL experiment in [[European Synchrotron Radiation Facility]] (Grenoble); the obtained limit became a reference number for Special Relativity extension models.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Gurzadyan, V. G. |author2=Margarian, A. T. |title=Inverse compton testing of fundamental physics and the cosmic background radiation|journal= Physica Scripta|volume=53|issue=5 |pages=513–515|year=1996|doi=10.1088/0031-8949/53/5/001|bibcode = 1996PhyS...53..513G|s2cid=250775347 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Gurzadyan V.G.|title=Lowering the light speed isotropy limit: European Synchrotron Radiation Facility measurements|journal= Il Nuovo Cimento B|volume=122|page=515|year=2007|issue=5|bibcode = 2007NCimB.122..515G|arxiv=astro-ph/0701127|display-authors=etal|doi=10.1393/ncb/i2007-10393-7|s2cid=15442487}}</ref><ref name=gm18>{{cite journal |author1=Gurzadyan, V.G. |author2=Margaryan, A.T. |title=The light speed versus the observer: the Kennedy–Thorndike test from GRAAL-ESRF|journal=Eur. Phys. J. C |volume=78|issue=8 |year=2018|page=607|doi=10.1140/epjc/s10052-018-6080-x|doi-access=free|arxiv=1807.08551|bibcode=2018EPJC...78..607G |s2cid=119374401 }}</ref>

== Other topics ==
Gurzadyan invented<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | year = 2005 | title = Kolmogorov complexity, string information, panspermia and the Fermi paradox| journal = Observatory | volume = 125 | pages = 352–355 | arxiv = physics/0508010| bibcode = 2005Obs...125..352G}}</ref> the concept of [[information panspermia]] which Webb<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Webb | first1 = S. | year = 2015 | title = If the Universe Is Teeming with Aliens... Where Is Everybody? | publisher= Springer |location=New York |isbn=978-3-319-13235-8 }}</ref> attributed as Solution 23 of the [[Fermi Paradox]]. That concept includes the hypothesis that the Universe can be full of traveling extraterrestrial life streams as low-complexity compressed bit strings at [[John von Neumann|von Neumann]] automata network. He has shown that human genome and hence the terrestrial life possess low [[Kolmogorov complexity]] and hence the corresponding bit strings can be transmitted by an [[Arecibo]]-type antenna to Galactic distances.

Gurzadyan and Penrose discussed [[information panspermia]]<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | last2 = Penrose | first2 = R. | year = 2016 | title = CCC and the Fermi paradox | journal = Eur. Phys. J. Plus | volume = 131 |  page = 11 | doi=10.1140/epjp/i2016-16011-1| arxiv = 1512.00554 | bibcode = 2016EPJP..131...11G | s2cid = 73537479 }}</ref> within the [[Conformal Cyclic Cosmology]], and the [[cosmic microwave background radiation]] transferring information from pre-Big Bang aeon to ours.

He led a study with geneticists in [[Duke University]] introducing a new method to detect somatic mutations in genomic sequences,<ref>{{cite journal|author= Gurzadyan, V. G.  |title=Detecting somatic mutations in genomic sequences by means of Kolmogorov–Arnold analysis|journal= Royal Society Open Science|volume=2|issue=8 |article-number=150143|year=2015|doi=10.1098/rsos.150143|doi-access=free|pmid=26361546 |pmc=4555851 |display-authors=etal|arxiv=1506.04080|bibcode=2015RSOS....250143G}}</ref> in proposing ''bath-quantum system'' viewpoint on the relation of thermodynamic and cosmological arrows of time.<ref>{{cite journal |last1 = Allahverdyan| first1 = A.E.|  last2 = Gurzadyan | first2 = V.G. | year = 2002 | title = Arrows of Time and Chaotic Properties of the Cosmic Background Radiation | journal =  Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General| volume = 35| issue = 34| pages = 7243–7254 |doi=10.1088/0305-4470/35/34/301| arxiv = astro-ph/0210022| bibcode = 2002JPhA...35.7243A}}</ref>

== Revealing the chronology of ancient world with astronomical dating ==
Gurzadyan's collaboration with archaeologists on the [[Chronology of the ancient Near East]]<ref>Gasche, H., Armstrong, J.A., Cole, S.W. and Gurzadyan, V.G., Dating the fall of Babylon: A Reappraisal of Second-millennium Chronology, University of Ghent and the Oriental Institute of the University of Chicago,1998.</ref> and his analysis of the [[Venus tablet of Ammisaduqa]] and of lunar eclipses of the [[Third Dynasty of Ur]] led to the introducing of the [[Chronology of the ancient Near East|Ultra-Low chronology]] of the 2nd-millennium ancient Near East.<ref>Gurzadyan V.G., "[http://www.arxiv.org/abs/physics/0311035 On the Astronomical Records and Babylonian Chronology]", ''Akkadica'', v.119-120, p.175 (2000); Gurzadyan V.G., [https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0311036] "The Venus Tablet and refraction.", ''Akkadica'' v.124, p.13 (2003); Gurzadyan V.G., [https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0311114] Astronomy and the Fall of Babylon, Sky & Telescope, v.100, No.1 (July), p.40 (2000); Gurzadyan V.G., Warburton D.A.,  [https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0607137] On the Available Lunar and Solar Eclipses and Babylonian Chronology, Akkadica, v.126, p.195 (2005).</ref>

He identified [[Halley's Comet]] depicted on ancient coins of Armenian king [[Tigranes the Great]], I c. BC. as the earliest known image of that comet<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Gurzadyan, V. G. |author2=Vardanyan, R. |title= Halley's comet of 87 BC on the coins of Armenian king Tigranes? |journal= Astronomy & Geophysics |volume=45|issue=4 |pages=4.06|year=2004 |doi=10.1046/j.1468-4004.2003.45406.x|arxiv=physics/0405073|bibcode=2004A&G....45d...6G|s2cid=119357985 }}</ref> He revealed the observation of supernova [[SN 1054]] (progenitor of [[Crab Nebula]]) in Armenian medieval chronicle of Hetum ([[Hayton of Corycus]]) and Cronaca Rampona.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | year = 2012 | title = The supernova of 1054 AD, the Armenian chronicle of Hetum, and Cronaca Rampona| journal = Observatory | volume = 132 | issue = 5| pages = 338–339 |bibcode = 2012Obs...132..338G | arxiv = 1207.3865}}</ref>

== Activities ==
Member of [[Euroscience]] Governing Board (elected in 1998, reelected in 2002). Chair of organizing committees of workshops such as "Ergodic Concepts in Stellar Dynamics", Geneva, 1993; "The Chaotic Universe", Rome, 1999; "Fermi and Astrophysics", Rome-Pescara, 2001; IX Marcel Grossmann meeting, Rome 2000, chair of 'Chaos' Parallel sessions at Marcel Grossmann Meetings, Jerusalem, 1997, Rome, 2000, Rio de Janeiro, 2003, Berlin, 2006. Paris, 2009. Co-editor of [[International Journal of Modern Physics D]] (World Scientific, 2000-2010), of [[The European Physical Journal Plus]] [[(Springer)]] and of book series 'Advances in Astronomy and Astrophysics' (Taylor & Francis, UK). Fellow of the Royal Astronomical Society (UK).

Speaker at XXII [[Solvay conference]] on physics, keynote speaker at IXth Swiss Biennial on Science, Technics + Aesthetics on "The Large, The Small and the Human Mind", lecturer at Xth Brazilian School of Cosmology and Gravitation.
